Hemoglobin.explanation_low: Low hemoglobin may relate to anemia.
Hemoglobin.explanation_high: High hemoglobin may indicate dehydration or elevated red blood cell production.

WBC.explanation_low: Low WBC may relate to reduced immune defense.
WBC.explanation_high: High WBC can occur with infections.

Platelets.explanation_low: Low platelets may relate to increased risk of bruising or bleeding.
Platelets.explanation_high: High platelets may relate to reactive inflammation or bone marrow response.

RBC.explanation_low: Low red blood cell count may be associated with anemia or fatigue.
RBC.explanation_high: High red blood cell count can occur with low oxygen levels or dehydration.

Hematocrit.explanation_low: Low hematocrit indicates a lower proportion of red blood cells in your blood.
Hematocrit.explanation_high: High hematocrit indicates a higher concentration of red blood cells.

MCV.explanation_low: Low MCV indicates smaller than average red blood cells.
MCV.explanation_high: High MCV indicates larger than average red blood cells.

MCH.explanation_low: Low MCH can occur in iron deficiency anemia.
MCH.explanation_high: High MCH can be seen in macrocytic anemias.

MCHC.explanation_low: Low MCHC indicates diluted hemoglobin concentration in red cells.
MCHC.explanation_high: High MCHC may suggest cell dehydration or spherocytosis.

RDW.explanation_low: Low RDW is clinically not significant.
RDW.explanation_high: High RDW indicates significant variation in red blood cell sizes.

Neutrophils.explanation_low: Low neutrophils can temporarily lower immune defense.
Neutrophils.explanation_high: Elevated neutrophils commonly accompany acute bacterial infections.

Lymphocytes.explanation_low: Low lymphocytes may be seen following viral illness or stress.
Lymphocytes.explanation_high: Elevated lymphocytes often occur in response to viral infections.

Monocytes.explanation_low: Low monocytes are rarely clinically significant.
Monocytes.explanation_high: Elevated monocytes can be seen with chronic inflammation or recovery.

Eosinophils.explanation_low: Low eosinophils are generally within normal baseline variation.
Eosinophils.explanation_high: Elevated eosinophils can relate to allergies or parasitic recovery.

Basophils.explanation_low: Low basophils are typical and expected.
Basophils.explanation_high: High basophils may accompany allergic reactions.

ESR.explanation_high: High ESR suggests inflammation somewhere in the body.

CRP.explanation_low: Normal CRP indicates no active acute inflammation.
CRP.explanation_high: Elevated CRP is a general marker of inflammation or infection.

Glucose.explanation_low: Low glucose may indicate hypoglycemia, which can cause lightheadedness.
Glucose.explanation_high: Elevated glucose may suggest impaired sugar metabolism or prediabetes.

HbA1c.explanation_low: Low HbA1c is generally within normal limits unless accompanied by frequent hypoglycemia.
HbA1c.explanation_high: Elevated HbA1c reflects higher average blood sugar levels over the past 3 months.

Creatinine.explanation_low: Low creatinine is usually not a concern and can relate to lower muscle mass.
Creatinine.explanation_high: Elevated creatinine may indicate that the kidneys are working harder to filter waste.

BUN.explanation_low: Low blood urea nitrogen is usually not medically significant.
BUN.explanation_high: Elevated BUN can be seen with dehydration, high protein intake, or reduced kidney clearance.

Total Cholesterol.explanation_low: Low total cholesterol is generally uncommon and rarely requires intervention.
Total Cholesterol.explanation_high: High total cholesterol indicates elevated blood lipid levels, which warrants lifestyle attention.

Triglycerides.explanation_high: High triglycerides suggest elevated circulating fats in the bloodstream.

LDL.explanation_high: High LDL cholesterol indicates elevated cardiovascular lipid markers.

HDL.explanation_low: Lower HDL cholesterol suggests lower protective lipid levels.
HDL.explanation_high: High HDL is considered protective for heart health.

Sodium.explanation_low: Low sodium may relate to fluid imbalance or overhydration.
Sodium.explanation_high: High sodium may indicate dehydration or high salt intake.

Potassium.explanation_low: Low potassium can affect muscle and nerve function.
Potassium.explanation_high: High potassium requires prompt clinical attention as it impacts heart rhythm.

Calcium.explanation_low: Low calcium can be related to vitamin D or dietary intake.
Calcium.explanation_high: High calcium can indicate parathyroid activity.

Total Protein.explanation_low: Low total protein may relate to nutritional or liver status.
Total Protein.explanation_high: High total protein can be associated with chronic inflammation.

Albumin.explanation_low: Low albumin can reflect liver production or nutritional status.
Albumin.explanation_high: High albumin is typically a sign of dehydration.

Bilirubin.explanation_high: High bilirubin can occur when the liver is processing red blood cells or bile flow is reduced.

ALT.explanation_low: Low ALT is normal and expected.
ALT.explanation_high: High ALT is a sensitive marker of liver enzyme activity.

AST.explanation_high: High AST indicates increased enzyme release from liver or muscle tissue.

ALP.explanation_high: High ALP can relate to bone metabolism or bile ducts.

Ferritin.explanation_low: Low ferritin indicates depleted iron storage in the body.
Ferritin.explanation_high: High ferritin can reflect inflammation or high iron stores.

TSH.explanation_low: Low TSH may indicate overactivity of the thyroid gland.
TSH.explanation_high: Elevated TSH may indicate an underactive thyroid response.

Vitamin D.explanation_low: Low vitamin D may relate to reduced bone health or insufficient sun exposure.
Vitamin D.explanation_high: High vitamin D is typically seen only with excessive supplementation.

Vitamin B12.explanation_low: Low vitamin B12 may cause fatigue or nerve sensations.
Vitamin B12.explanation_high: High vitamin B12 is usually not harmful and often reflects dietary intake.
